item.title: Ion-Regulated Interfacial Solvation Enables Ether Electrolytes for 4.4 V Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:
تنظیم سولواسیون بینسطحی با یونهای K+ و BH4- در الکترولیت اتری، پایداری آند لیتیوم و پنجره اکسیداسیون را افزایش داده و باتری Li-NCM811 با ولتاژ 4.4 V را ممکن میسازد.
ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using K+ and BH4– to selectively tailor interfacial solvation, rather than bulk solvation, enabling ether electrolytes for 4.4 V lithium metal batteries. This approach suppresses interfacial decomposition, extends Li plating/stripping to 160 cycles, raises oxidation onset to 5.00 V, and retains 85.7% capacity after 100 cycles in NCM811 full cells.
🏷 lithium metal battery · ether electrolyte · interfacial solvation · KBH4 additive · high-voltage NCM811

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work identifies intrinsic limits on spent LiCoO₂ recovery and uses lattice reconstruction plus a nanoscale rock-salt surface layer to regenerate high-voltage cathodes. The strategy restores layered structure and Li⁺ kinetics, enabling stable 4.6 V cycling (81% retention after 1500 cycles). It offers a scalable route for high-value battery recycling.

💡 The novelty lies in using Al³⁺ in situ substitution in a concentrated electrolyte to fill Mn dissolution vacancies and form stable Al–N bonds, creating a gradient KMnPBA cathode. Interdisciplinary Materials | 💭 Perspective | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This perspective reframes pressure as a compensatory crutch, not a solution, and identifies chemo-mechanical mismatch as the root cause of low-pressure ASSLSB degradation. It proposes design principles—reaction accessibility, adaptive ion-conducting phases, and stable interfaces—shifting focus from accommodating pressure to eliminating pressure dependence, a critical step for practical high-energy solid-state batteries.
